label: token x in the original (pre-<DEL>) input
explanation: Token detector for the letter x. It fires on every original-phase step whose input is x (precision 1.0 on dev), and on essentially nothing else. Activations are strongest at the last original position (around 0.97-1.0 of max, right before <DEL>) and at early positions. They are weakest in the middle of longer sequences (around 0.6-0.7). It is mostly silent when x is re-input during the copy phase: only weak traces (about 0.15 of max) remain there, mainly at recall_idx 1 when the sequence began with x. These copy-phase traces and a few stray weak activations on other tokens (o, n, 3) hold under 0.3% of the activation mass. It does not depend on the previous token, on L, or on which token is being output.

issues: Minor only: the explanation's own numbers are internally consistent with the profile. On test, precision is 1.0 with 0 false positives, and all 1528 missed steps hold 0.3% of the activation mass. Most misses are weak (about 0.15 of max) copy-phase activations at recall_idx 1, where the re-input is x because the sequence began with x. The rest are a few stray weak activations, e.g. on n.

Magnitude claims confirmed from the examples: last original position (to_go 0) is about 0.97-1.0 of max, position 0 is about 0.95, and the middle of long sequences is about 0.6-0.7. 'Does not depend on prev token or L' holds for firing rate, since rate is flat across prev_tok and L. Magnitude may shift with these slightly, but that does not affect the label.
